question: Find the L.C.M. of. (4)/(7), (5)/(21) and(8)/(63).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

L.C.M. of fractions = L.C.M. of Numerators ÷ H.C.F. of Denominators

Numerators are 4, 5, and 8 ⇒ L.C.M.(4, 5, 8) = 40

Denominators are 7, 21, and 63 ⇒ H.C.F.(7, 21, 63) = 7

Required L.C.M. = 40/7

**∴ The correct answer is 40/7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The fractions are 4/7, 5/21, and 8/63.

**Formula Used:**

L.C.M. of fractions = L.C.M. of Numerators ÷ H.C.F. of Denominators

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, we find the L.C.M. of the numerators (4, 5, and 8).

⇒ Prime factorization of 4 = 2²

⇒ Prime factorization of 5 = 5¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 8 = 2³

⇒ L.C.M.(4, 5, 8) = 2³ × 5 = 8 × 5 = 40

⇒ Next, we find the H.C.F. of the denominators (7, 21, and 63).

⇒ Prime factorization of 7 = 7¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 21 = 3¹ × 7¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 63 = 3² × 7¹

⇒ H.C.F.(7, 21, 63) = 7

⇒ Now, applying the formula: L.C.M. of fractions = 40 ÷ 7 = 40/7

**∴ The correct answer is 40/7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

H.C.F. of Fractions

To find the Highest Common Factor of fractions, use the formula: H.C.F. of fractions = H.C.F. of Numerators ÷ L.C.M. of Denominators.

Product of Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b, the product of their L.C.M. and H.C.F. is equal to the product of the numbers themselves: L.C.M.(a, b) × H.C.F.(a, b) = a × b.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers do not have any common prime factors, they are called co-prime numbers. Their H.C.F. is always 1, and their L.C.M. is simply their product.
